summary: Recovered and compared the original paper, completed three bounded search families, and read two additional primary works. Located a cumulative-count recurrence and clarified its relation to exact maximum-displacement counts. No all-n resolution or certification is claimed.
report:
The supplied implementation documents were read in the declared order. The task, charter, fresh-start policy and empty knowledge/source catalogs supplied the baseline; no prior-instance research was used. This submits the investigation for research_plan assessment of literature-original, literature-followups and literature-handoff, without declaring task completion.

Original: pinned PDFs, extracted text, inspected images and retrieval hashes are preserved under primary-files/. The [v1 paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.07243v1) was read on pp.1-6,23-24; v2 on pp.1,3,23. The inspected definitions identify the charter’s statistic and exact-count sequence. The September 2026 revision retains Conjecture 6.5. source-dossier.json records version distinctions, formula coordinates, visually confirmed wording inconsistencies and unread ranges. The inconsistencies do not refute unimodality.

Additional works: two were selected, below the cap of three. Aguilar-Fraga et al., [Interval and ℓ-interval rational parking functions](https://doi.org/10.46298/dmtcs.12598), publisher PDF pp.1-6,8-10, supplies the cumulative recurrence in Theorem 3.7 (p.8), with proof through p.9. Its formula and cumulative table were visually checked. This is primary background from 2024, not a later resolution. Selig and Zhu, [Parking functions and Łukasiewicz paths](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2024.070), journal pp.77-81, supplies Theorem 2.1 (p.80): maximum displacement corresponds to path height on nondecreasing parking functions. The displayed domain and equality were visually checked. No transfer to arbitrary preference orderings is asserted.

Coverage: bounded-search-log.json records actual queries, syntax, ordering, offsets, totals, inspected identifiers, selection reasons and stopping conditions. The title family inspected ten Crossref records after an arXiv 429; the conjecture-number/unimodality family inspected the first ten of 25 OpenAlex records; the maximum-displacement family inspected all six returned OpenAlex records after a zbMATH 404. No further pages were inspected. Unselected works remain content-unchecked. No all-n solution was identified in these windows and read passages; this does not establish literature-wide absence.

Retrieval: scholarly tools became callable after initial discovery, so the provisional missing-tool inference and operations request were withdrawn. Actual scholarly arXiv searches/fetches returned HTTP 429 without Retry-After. A PDF-only request still entered the adapter’s metadata preflight. Browser access and explicit public downloads subsequently recovered both pinned PDFs; this fallback is distinguished from successful scholarly retrieval. Additional publisher PDFs, source responses and manifests remain in scholarly-data/.

One early self-check response was rejected as research_action_before_response after a checkpoint-read command; support-observation.json preserves that historical rejection. The subsequent interval self-check was accepted. The local submission checker passed with no structural issues; this does not establish central acceptance, mathematical validity or task completion.

These findings are nonformal literature observations. No Lean code was submitted: the task requests source investigation, and no verified K definition was supplied on which to build a formal result.

knowledge.title: Checked identification of Conjecture 6.5 with the charter
knowledge.statement: In the inspected original-paper passages, maxdisp is the charter’s M and |IPF_n(k)^max| is b_{n,k}; |IPF_n(k)| instead counts M≤k.
knowledge.explanation: See source-dossier.json and the preserved v1 PDF, Definitions 2.5 and 2.7 (p.3), Conjecture 6.5 (p.23) and Table 1 (p.24); relevant v2 passages were also checked. These are source-reading observations, not a certified theorem. The dossier preserves transcription cautions and unread ranges.
knowledge.summary: The conjecture concerns exact maximum displacement, with matching cutoff parameter k.

knowledge.title: Primary cumulative recurrence for displacement cutoffs
knowledge.statement: Aguilar-Fraga et al., Theorem 3.7, states A_0(k)=1 and A_n(k)=Σ_{x=0}^{n−1} binom(n−1,x) min(x+1,k+1) A_x(k) A_{n−1−x}(k), where n≥1, k≥0 and A_n(k)=|IPF_n(k)|.
knowledge.explanation: The publisher PDF at scholarly-data/blobs/062a21f50827c0c73996b8f9c5a364c2c88b48a27441393c1a620fbcf529dbdb was read at pp.8-9, including the last-car partition proof; its formula and table were visually checked. The paper defines N to include zero. Specialize its number of spots to m=n. A counts displacement at most k; for the charter’s n≥1, define A_n(-1)=0 and obtain exact counts by A_n(k)-A_n(k-1). This comparison follows the matching definitions; the recurrence still needs an independent proof and formal verification before certified reuse.
knowledge.summary: A primary recurrence computes cumulative counts; unimodality of their first differences remains unproved here.

knowledge.title: Nondecreasing restriction of the maximum-displacement path theorem
knowledge.statement: Selig-Zhu Theorem 2.1 identifies maximum displacement with Łukasiewicz-path height for nondecreasing parking functions; it is not a theorem about all preference orderings.
knowledge.explanation: The publisher PDF at scholarly-data/blobs/7c35016e1759a69900ac4ce69168e3cf4edc9ac8818962b18bf7f668bbdc9f80 was read at journal pp.77-81. Theorem 2.1 and Equation (2) on p.80 were visually checked. The map records preference multiplicities, ell_i=#{j:p_j=i}-1, and its bijection domain is PF_n^inc. No statistic-preserving transfer to all ordered preference lists was established in this investigation.
knowledge.summary: The path-height interpretation is restricted evidence; the full-PF bridge remains open.
